story.title: OPERATION BLACKOUT
story.briefing: ALERT: At 02:00 hours, NovaCorp Industries regional power grid was compromised by an elite adversarial entity known as 'SHADOW-X'. Digital forensics confirm the attack was facilitated by an insider with high-level access. You are deployed as the ethical-hacking digital response team. Analyze the breadcrumbs, dismantle the attack chain, unmask the insider, and abort the blackout sequence before the grid fails.
story.entryTransmission:
INTERCEPTED TRANSMISSION // SOURCE: UNKNOWN // CHANNEL 0x7F //
... [SYS_ALERT]: RECON UNIT DETECTED. ENCRYPTED ACCESS CODE DISCOVERED IN BASE64 FRAGMENT: 'R1JJRC0yMDI2' ...
DECODE TO UNLOCK THE GRID ENTRY GATE.

levels.title: Reconnaissance
levels.subtitle: Find the Hidden Information
levels.description: Investigate NovaCorp's public-facing staging portal. Extract intelligence hidden within developer comments, server configuration, DNS records, and asset metadata.

hints.text: Inspect the HTML source code comments and check standard crawler control files like robots.txt.
Look at the DNS TXT record response. Base64 strings often end with '=' or '=='.
The flag format is NIGHT{...}. Check the image metadata EXIF author tag or combine the recon fragments.

reconData.htmlSource:
NovaCorp Grid Substation #4

Status: All relays online.
reconData.robotsTxt:
User-agent: *
Disallow: /admin-secret-portal/
Disallow: /backups/config.bak
# Staging Notice: Developer flag marker is NIGHT{RECON_MASTER}

ethicalHackerNote.howDefendersFix: Defenders secure public surfaces by stripping metadata from published media, ensuring robots.txt does not leak sensitive administrative paths, sanitizing HTML debug comments during CI/CD build pipelines, and regularly auditing public DNS TXT records.
ethicalHackerNote.permissionNotice: Always obtain explicit, documented authorization from asset owners before enumerating DNS or inspecting non-public web resources.

quiz.question: What is the primary objective of robots.txt on a public web server?
options: It acts as a firewall rule that cryptographically restricts unauthorized visitors.
It is an advisory standard instructing web crawlers which paths not to index.
It executes server-side authentication scripts for privileged accounts.
It encrypts internal directory trees from search engines.
quiz.explanation: robots.txt is purely advisory for search crawlers. Attackers frequently read it to discover unlinked or sensitive directories.

quiz.question: Which DNS record type commonly stores domain verification, SPF email policies, and text tokens?
options: A Record
CNAME Record
TXT Record
PTR Record
quiz.explanation: TXT records hold arbitrary text and are widely used for SPF, DKIM, and domain ownership tokens.

quiz.question: Why should images uploaded to enterprise portals have EXIF metadata scrubbed?
options: EXIF data can leak sensitive geolocation coordinates, camera serial numbers, and creator usernames.
EXIF data automatically disables TLS encryption on images.
Removing EXIF increases image resolution.
EXIF metadata causes browsers to crash on mobile devices.
quiz.explanation: EXIF metadata can disclose GPS coordinates, software versions, and internal usernames of the creators.

levels.title: Web Security
levels.subtitle: Break the Web
levels.description: Bypass an insecure authentication portal using simulated SQL injection, then manipulate insecure client-side session cookies to escalate privileges to Administrator.

hints.text: For the login bypass, use a classic SQL injection payload that makes the WHERE clause always true, e.g. ' OR '1'='1
Once inside the operator console, examine the in-game Cookie Editor panel. What role are you currently assigned?
Change the 'role' cookie value from 'user' to 'admin' and click 'Save & Reload Cookie' to claim the flag.

sqlChallenge.simulatedQuery: SELECT * FROM operators WHERE username = '${INPUT_USER}' AND password = '${INPUT_PASS}'

ethicalHackerNote.skill: SQL Injection (SQLi) & Broken Object Level Authorization / Client-Side State Tampering
ethicalHackerNote.howDefendersFix: Defenders eliminate SQLi by using Parameterized Queries (Prepared Statements) or ORMs that treat user input strictly as data rather than executable code. Client-side state tampering is prevented by storing privileges server-side in signed sessions or cryptographically validated JWTs with HttpOnly and Secure cookie flags.
ethicalHackerNote.permissionNotice: Attempting SQL injection against any production server without explicit written consent is illegal under computer misuse legislation.

quiz.question: Which programming technique completely eliminates SQL Injection vulnerabilities?
options: Writing longer and more complex SQL queries.
Using Parameterized Queries (Prepared Statements) with bound parameters.
Converting all database strings into Base64 format.
Switching database ports from 3306 to 8080.
quiz.explanation: Prepared statements ensure the database engine never interprets user-supplied strings as executable SQL command syntax.

quiz.question: What does the 'HttpOnly' flag on a cookie accomplish?
options: It restricts the cookie from being sent over HTTPS connections.
It prevents client-side JavaScript (e.g. document.cookie) from accessing the cookie, mitigating XSS session theft.
It forces the browser to compress the cookie payload.
It allows the cookie to be shared across any third-party domain.
quiz.explanation: HttpOnly blocks client-side scripts from reading session cookies, protecting session tokens from Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).

quiz.question: Why is relying on client-side cookies like 'role=admin' fundamentally flawed?
options: Cookies can only hold numbers, not text.
The client controls their browser and can modify, forge, or tamper with any cookie value.
Browsers automatically delete cookies after every HTTP request.
Cookies only work on desktop browsers.
quiz.explanation: Any data sent from or stored on the client is untrusted. Authorization roles must be verified securely on the server.

levels.title: Cryptography
levels.subtitle: Decode the Secret
levels.description: Intercept an encrypted transmission left behind on the command bus. Reverse a multi-stage cipher (Hex -> Base64 -> Caesar) and decode an audio Morse code transmission to construct the full verification flag.

hints.text: The layered ciphertext is Hex-encoded. Convert Hex to ASCII text first using the Decoder Toolkit.
The resulting string is Base64. Decode Base64 to reveal text that has been shifted by Caesar ROT+3 (Shift = 3).
The audio player emits Morse code for letters S-H-A-D-O-W (... .... .- -.. --- .--). Append _SHADOW to CYBER_DEFENSE_GRID!

ethicalHackerNote.skill: Multi-Stage Cryptanalysis, Encoding Differentiation & Audio Signal Decoding
ethicalHackerNote.howDefendersFix: Defenders never rely on 'security through obscurity' or weak classical ciphers like Caesar / ROT. Production systems must utilize industry-standard, mathematically validated cryptography such as AES-256-GCM, TLS 1.3, and Edwards-curve signatures (Ed25519) with robust key management.
ethicalHackerNote.permissionNotice: Ethical hackers analyze and stress-test encryption standards under strict rules of engagement, adhering to responsible vulnerability disclosure.

quiz.question: What is the crucial difference between encoding (such as Base64 or Hex) and encryption (such as AES)?
options: Encoding protects data confidentiality, while encryption only compresses data.
Encoding transforms data representation without requiring a secret key; encryption protects secrecy using a secret cryptographic key.
Encoding can only be performed on numbers, while encryption works on text.
There is no difference; they are identical concepts.
quiz.explanation: Encoding is for data interchange and is easily reversed by anyone without a key. Encryption requires a secret key to decipher.

quiz.question: Why is the classic Caesar cipher considered completely insecure for modern data protection?
options: It requires quantum supercomputers to decrypt.
It has a keyspace of only 25 possible shifts, making brute-force cracking trivial within milliseconds.
It only works on ancient Latin text.
It cannot encrypt lowercase characters.
quiz.explanation: With only 25 possible alphabetic shifts, an attacker can test all keys instantaneously or use letter frequency analysis.

quiz.question: In modern symmetric encryption, what is the role of an Initialization Vector (IV) or Nonce?
options: It replaces the secret encryption key.
It ensures that encrypting identical plaintexts with the same key produces completely distinct ciphertexts.
It acts as a digital copyright mark.
It speeds up network transmission bandwidth.
quiz.explanation: A unique IV/nonce prevents attackers from recognizing patterns when identical plaintexts are encrypted multiple times.

levels.title: Malware Hunter
levels.subtitle: Hunt the Malicious Artifact
levels.description: Inspect live system telemetry from the compromised substation controller. Identify the masquerading executable, isolate the Command & Control (C2) domain, and uncover the persistence registry key.

hints.text: Check the Process List carefully. Look for a process with typosquatting/masquerading (e.g. 0 instead of o).
Inspect the Network & Auth Log tab. Find the external domain name receiving beaconing traffic on port 8443.
Check the Persistence Script tab. Locate the Registry Run value name being added.

malwareArtifacts.persistenceScript:
# NovaCorp Emergency Update Dispatcher (Tampered)
$TargetReg = 'HKCU:\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run'
$MalwarePath = 'C:\Users\Public\svch0st.exe'
Set-ItemProperty -Path $TargetReg -Name 'WinUpdateHelper' -Value "$MalwarePath -c2 c2-darknode.internal"
Write-Output 'Persistence established under WinUpdateHelper.'

ethicalHackerNote.skill: Endpoint Forensics, Process Masquerading Detection & Persistence Triage
ethicalHackerNote.howDefendersFix: Defenders counter malware execution by enforcing Application Whitelisting (AppLocker/WDAC), restricting script execution in user-writable paths like C:\Users\Public, deploying Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) sensors to alert on suspicious Run registry edits, and implementing DNS sinkholes for malicious C2 domains.
ethicalHackerNote.permissionNotice: Malware analysis must always be executed in quarantined, isolated sandboxes without external internet routing.

quiz.question: What is the security term for naming a malicious binary 'svch0st.exe' to mimic the legitimate 'svchost.exe'?
options: Process Masquerading / Typosquatting
Buffer Overflow
Cross-Site Scripting
Man-in-the-Middle
quiz.explanation: Masquerading (MITRE ATT&CK T1036) manipulates file names or paths to evade human review and rudimentary process monitoring.

quiz.question: Which Windows registry hive is commonly abused to automatically execute malware upon user login?
options: HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\HardwareProfiles
HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run
HKCU\Control Panel\Desktop\Colors
HKLM\SECURITY\Cache
quiz.explanation: The CurrentVersion\Run registry key specifies applications that start automatically whenever a user logs into Windows.

quiz.question: In cybersecurity incident response, what is a 'C2' or 'C&C' server?
options: A server that compiles C++ code for developers.
A Command and Control infrastructure controlled by attackers to remotely manage compromised implants and exfiltrate data.
A backup database server used for disaster recovery.
A cryptographic certification authority.
quiz.explanation: Command and Control (C2) servers allow adversaries to issue instructions, deploy secondary payloads, and pull stolen data from victims.

levels.title: The Final Vault
levels.subtitle: Unmask the Insider & Restore the Grid
levels.description: Synthesize the four evidence fragments gathered across the incident investigation. Input the insider's employee credential ID and the adversary's alias to trigger the Master Override Sequence.

hints.text: Combine the evidence fragments from Level 1, Level 2, and Level 3: EMP + 44 + 71 -> EMP-4471.
The adversary alias was gathered in Level 4: SHADOW-X.
Submit Insider ID 'EMP-4471' and Hacker Alias 'SHADOW-X' to unmask the rogue architect.

ethicalHackerNote.skill: Root Cause Analysis, Threat Attribution & Forensic Synthesis
ethicalHackerNote.howDefendersFix: Defenders prevent insider threats through the Principle of Least Privilege, Separation of Duties, robust PAM (Privileged Access Management), automated behavioral analytics (UEBA), and multi-party authorization for critical infrastructure commands.
ethicalHackerNote.permissionNotice: Attribution and incident response play vital roles in defending critical infrastructure within legal and ethical boundaries.

quiz.question: Which principle limits employee access strictly to the resources necessary for their specific job role?
options: Principle of Least Privilege (PoLP)
Security Through Obscurity
Open Door Policy
Default Allow Architecture
quiz.explanation: Least Privilege ensures that even if an account is compromised or turns rogue, the blast radius is strictly confined.

quiz.question: What is UEBA in modern enterprise defense?
options: Universal Ethernet Bus Adapter
User and Entity Behavior Analytics, which uses machine learning to detect anomalous activities indicative of insider threats.
Unified Encryption Backup Architecture
Unrestricted External Browser Access
quiz.explanation: UEBA monitors baseline user behaviors and triggers alarms when anomalous data transfers or access spikes occur.

quiz.question: Why is multi-party authorization (dual-custody) essential for critical infrastructure operations?
options: It ensures no single rogue individual can unilaterally trigger catastrophic actions like shutting down a power grid.
It slows down computer boot time.
It doubles electricity consumption.
It prevents computers from using passwords.
quiz.explanation: Dual-custody requires independent verification from two authorized parties, preventing single-point insider compromises.
